subject.title: Granola 7.427.2 moved the DEK from storage.dek into the macOS Keychain — encrypted-json/private-api unlock fails with "read storage.dek: no such file or directory"

question: Should graincrawl stop at an actionable unsupported-Keychain diagnostic, or should it pursue a Granola-authorized mechanism for recovering the migrated DEK on packaged macOS builds?
rationale: The immediate error message can be improved mechanically, but recovering the key from an access-group-protected Keychain item determines whether the project will cross an upstream application security boundary.

options.title: Ship diagnosis only
options.body: Detect the migrated-Keychain condition and explain that encrypted-json/private-api unlock is unavailable on affected Granola builds until a supported bridge exists.

options.title: Design an authorized bridge
options.body: Investigate a Granola-supported companion or export path, with explicit security review, before adding any capability that accesses the migrated DEK.

recommendation.title: Ship diagnosis only
recommendation.body: Detect the migrated-Keychain condition and explain that encrypted-json/private-api unlock is unavailable on affected Granola builds until a supported bridge exists.
